decisions.reason: The existing same-message Event adds retail food-service and sanitation scope but incorrectly drops the previously active live-event, matcha-mixing, and cleaning contexts, which the source does not remove.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Larry, The latest updates are looking great. Seeing the plumbing, drainage routing, bowl integration, and overall structure come together has me even more excited about where this is heading. As I’ve been thinking ahead, one thing that keeps coming to mind is the possibility of eventually using the Matcha Mixer in a retail location if we move forward with opening a shop. Because of that, I wanted to start thinking about food-service and health department considerations early while we’re still in the prototype stage. A few things I’d love to keep in mind as the build progresses: 
 Food-contact materials (stainless steel, food-grade plastics, food-grade silicone, etc.) Ease of cleaning and sanitation Making sure there aren’t any hidden areas where liquid can collect or become trapped Easy removal of bowls, whisks, and components for cleaning Separation between liquids and electrical components Accessibility for maintenance and servicing if something ever needs to be replaced When you get a chance, I’d also love to know what materials are being used in the food-contact areas and whether there are any areas you see as potential sanitation or cleaning challenges. Long term, I think it would be helpful to keep documentation on: 
 materials used CAD files wiring layout cleaning procedures exploded-view drawings if available Not because we need all of that right now, but because if this evolves into something bigger, having that information could be incredibly valuable. Overall, everything is looking fantastic and I’m really excited to see the testing videos and final assembly. It’s amazing seeing the project move from an idea into a real machine. 

Karla Burton

decisions.reason: The existing message-176 MODIFY already captures the required sanitation, liquid-trap prevention, and food-service scope for the fluid path.
The existing message-176 MODIFY already extends the maintenance-access Requirement to food-service use while preserving its maintenance context.
The existing message-176 MODIFY already records the required separation between liquids and electrical components and the retail food-service context.
The source discusses sanitation, removable components, and service access but does not change splash-control behavior or scope.
Easy whisk removal for cleaning does not change the required mixing texture, foam quality, or high-speed mixing behavior.
The request for easy bowl removal and sanitation does not alter bowl capacity, size, or form.
The sanitation and removable-component request does not change spout geometry, orientation, construction, or pour direction.
The source does not change valve operation, button interaction, flow behavior, or the dispensing sequence; cleaning concerns are owned by separate sanitation Requirements.
The source requests awareness of food-contact materials and suggests retaining documentation long term, but it does not revise the approved component set or require a new BOM at this stage.
Whisk removability and sanitation considerations do not alter the platform height, footprint, or cup-clearance requirements.
The source describes retained CAD documentation as potentially helpful long term and explicitly says it is not needed now, so it does not modify the current system-layout or CAD deliverable.
